title: The Vector of New Lagos Again
premise: Rafael Halloran, a terraformer hauling seed-stock through the contested orbits of New Lagos, intercepts a distress signal broadcast in a language extinct since the Founding Wars — and recognizes it as the tongue his dead mother sang to him. The signal comes from a derelict colony ship holding the last living speakers of that language, refugees the war fleets on both sides want silenced because their testimony proves the war was manufactured. Pursued by a naval captain who was once his brother-in-arms, Rafael must smuggle the refugees' recorded message through the jump window before it closes, choosing between the found family he's built aboard his ship and a justice that will cost him his anonymity forever. He delivers the message — broadcast to every fleet at once — ending the war but burning his old life to ash, and he plants his final garden not for the unborn, but for the survivors who finally have a future.
about_author: Mirabel Voss is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals for deep-space freight contracts before turning to fiction. She writes science fiction about people whose jobs keep civilizations running and whose names never make the histories.

chapters.title: The Garden That Waits
chapters.summary: Rafael Halloran's POV. Fifteen years into tending a seed-vault garden for colonists not yet born, Rafael hauls cargo through contested orbits, invisible by design. When a distress signal arrives in a language extinct for two centuries — the lullaby-language his mother sang — his carefully buried past cracks open. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness pierced by a grief he thought he'd finished mourning.

chapters.title: Ghosts in the Derelict
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, with an interlude from refugee elder Sefa. Boarding the drifting colony ship, Rafael finds survivors of a purge both fleets officially deny, carrying a recorded testimony that proves the war was manufactured. His first mate, Iyo, urges him to walk away; Rafael can't. Emotional beat: found family forming under threat, as strangers become kin through shared language.

chapters.title: The Jump Window Closes
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Rafael and Captain Ondine Reyes, his former comrade now ordered to silence the refugees. Reyes corners Rafael's ship at the edge of the jump window, offering him amnesty if he surrenders the testimony. Betrayed by a trusted contact, Rafael loses his cargo, his cover, and nearly Iyo. Emotional beat: the price of survival made explicit — every safe thing stripped away.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Rafael and Reyes POV in alternation. Outgunned, Rafael chooses not to flee but to transmit the refugees' testimony to every fleet at once, using the garden's seed-relay array. Reyes, confronted with proof she fought a manufactured war, stands down her guns. The war collapses; Rafael, exposed and unmoored, plants a new garden — this one for the living. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, grief transmuted into rootedness.
